ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كهيعص (١)).
We have given the discussion of the disconnected letters (al-ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿa) at the beginning of [Sūrat] al-Baqara, so let it be consulted there.
His saying, Exalted is He: (عص): it is read with the nūn concealed (ikhfāʾ) before the ṣād, because of its closeness to it and their sharing in [the quality of] being understood [together]. [Translator's note: «فِي الْفَهْمِ» as written; possibly «فِي الْفَمِ», "in [being articulated in] the mouth".]
And it is read with it pronounced distinctly (iẓhār), because with the disconnected letters the intention is to distinguish them from one another, signalling that they are disconnected; for this reason some made a slight pause on each of their letters, and pronouncing the nūn distinctly signals that.

ukberi-tibyan:2-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ عَبْدَهُ زَكَرِيَّا (٢) إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ نِدَاءً خَفِيًّا (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذِكْرُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ): concerning its being nominative there are three views. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "this is a mention". The second: it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "among what is recited to you is a mention". The third: it is the khabar of the disconnected letters; al-Farrāʾ mentioned this, and it is far-fetched, because the khabar is the mubtadaʾ in meaning, and the disconnected letters contain no mention of the mercy, nor does the mention of the mercy have their meaning.
And (ذِكْرُ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) annexed to its object, the implied form being "this is that your Lord mentioned the mercy of His servant". [Translator's note: «إِنْ» in «هَذَا إِنْ ذَكَرَ» appears to stand for «أَنْ»; translated accordingly.]
It is also said: it is annexed to the agent by extension (ittisāʿ), the meaning being "this is that you mention the mercy of your Lord". On the first [view] «عَبْدَهُ» is made accusative by «رَحْمَة», and on the second by «ذِكْر».
It is read, among the irregular readings (shādhdh), «ذَكَرَ» as a past verb, with «رَحْمَةَ» as object and «عَبْدُهُ» as agent.
And (زَكَرِيَّا): a badal (substitute) from «عَبْدَهُ» on both views.
And it is read with the kāf doubled [«ذَكَّرَ»], with «رَحْمَةَ» and «عَبْدَهُ» in the accusative, i.e. "this Qurʾān reminded the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, or the community".
And (إِذْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for «الرَّحْمَة», or for «ذِكْر».

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي وَهَنَ الْعَظْمُ مِنِّي وَاشْتَعَلَ الرَّأْسُ شَيْبًا وَلَمْ أَكُنْ بِدُعَائِكَ رَبِّ شَقِيًّا (٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شَيْبًا): accusative as a tamyīz (specification). It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also said: it is accusative as a maṣdar [absolute object] from the meaning of «اشْتَعَلَ», because its meaning is "became grey".
And (بِدُعَائِكَ): a maṣdar annexed to its object, i.e. "by my calling upon You".

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنِّي خِفْتُ الْمَوَالِيَ مِنْ وَرَائِي وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا فَهَبْ لِي مِنْ لَدُنْكَ وَلِيًّا (٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خِفْتُ الْمَوَالِيَ): there is an omitted muḍāf (first term of the construct) in it, i.e. "the absence of kinsmen" or "the injustice of kinsmen".
It is also read «خَفَّتْ», with doubling and sukūn on the tāʾ, with «الْمَوَالِي» as the agent, i.e. "their number diminished".
The majority [read] with lengthening (madd) and the yāʾ kept in «وَرَائِي». And it is read with shortening (qaṣr) and fatḥa on the yāʾ [«وَرَايَ»]; this is a case of shortening a word ending in a long alif-hamza (qaṣr al-mamdūd).

ukberi-tibyan:6-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَرِثُنِي وَيَرِثُ مِنْ آلِ يَعْقُوبَ وَاجْعَلْهُ رَبِّ رَضِيًّا (٦) يَازَكَرِيَّا إِنَّا نُبَشِّرُكَ بِغُلَامٍ اسْمُهُ يَحْيَى لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ سَمِيًّا (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَرِثُنِي): it is read with the jussive in both [verbs] as the apodosis (jawāb), i.e. "if You grant, he will inherit"; and with the nominative in both as an adjective (ṣifa) of «وَلِيّ». This is stronger than the first, because he asked for an heir with this description, and the jussive does not yield this meaning.
It has been read irregularly (shādhdh): «يَرِثُنِي وَارِثٌ», on the basis that it is an active participle.
And (رَضِيًّا): i.e. «مَرْضِيًّا» (well-pleasing). It is also said: «رَاضِيًا» (content). The final radical (lām) of the word is wāw; this has preceded.
And (سَمِيًّا): of the pattern «فَعِيل» in the sense of «مُسَامِيًا» (a peer); the final radical of the word is wāw, from «سَمَا يَسْمُو».

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَكَانَتِ امْرَأَتِي عَاقِرًا وَقَدْ بَلَغْتُ مِنَ الْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا (٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عِتِيًّا): its original is «عُتُوّ», of the pattern «فُعُول», like «قُعُود» and «جُلُوس»; but they found the succession of two ḍammas and two wāws heavy, so they gave the tāʾ a kasra; the wāw then turned into yāʾ because of its being quiescent and preceded by a kasra, and then the wāw which is the final radical was turned into yāʾ because the first preceded it with sukūn.
Some of them give the ʿayn a kasra by assimilation (itbāʿ).
And it is read with fatḥa on it [the ʿayn], on the basis that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of the pattern «فَعِيل»; likewise «بُكِيّ» and «صِلِيّ». It is accusative by «بَلَغْتُ», i.e. "I have reached extreme age from old age", that is, because of old age. It [«مِنَ الْكِبَرِ»] may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عِتِيّ», or be attached to «بَلَغْتُ».
It is also said: «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), and «عِتِيًّا» is an emphasising maṣdar, or a tamyīz (specification), or a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl from the agent.

ukberi-tibyan:9-9.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ كَذَلِكَ قَالَ رَبُّكَ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ وَقَدْ خَلَقْتُكَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ تَكُ شَيْئًا (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قَالَ كَذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is thus".
It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "I shall do the like of what you have asked", and it is an allusion (kināya) to what he asked for.

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ رَبِّ اجْعَلْ لِي آيَةً قَالَ آيَتُكَ أَلَّا تُكَلِّمَ النَّاسَ ثَلَاثَ لَيَالٍ سَوِيًّا (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَوِيًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in «تُكَلِّمَ».

ukberi-tibyan:11-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَخَرَجَ عَلَى قَوْمِهِ مِنَ الْمِحْرَابِ فَأَوْحَى إِلَيْهِمْ أَنْ سَبِّحُوا بُكْرَةً وَعَشِيًّا (١١) يَايَحْيَى خُذِ الْكِتَابَ بِقُوَّةٍ وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحُكْمَ صَبِيًّا (١٢) وَحَنَانًا مِنْ لَدُنَّا وَزَكَاةً وَكَانَ تَقِيًّا (١٣) وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ جَبَّارًا عَصِيًّا (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ سَبِّحُوا): «أَنْ» may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), or in the sense of «أَيْ» (that is, explicative). And (بِقُوَّةٍ): an object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial). (وَحَنَانًا): conjoined to «الْحُكْمَ», i.e. "and We granted him tenderness". It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). And (بَرًّا): i.e. "and We made him dutiful". It is also said: it is conjoined to the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاذْكُرْ فِي الْكِتَابِ مَرْيَمَ إِذِ انْتَبَذَتْ مِنْ أَهْلِهَا مَكَانًا شَرْقِيًّا (١٦) فَاتَّخَذَتْ مِنْ دُونِهِمْ حِجَابًا فَأَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْهَا رُوحَنَا فَتَمَثَّلَ لَهَا بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذِ انْتَبَذَتْ): concerning «إِذْ» there are four views. The first: it is an adverb (ẓarf), and what governs it is omitted, its implied form being "and mention the story of Mary when she withdrew". The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the omitted muḍāf (first term of the construct). The third: it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "and make clear [the time] when she withdrew", so it belongs to another sentence, as Sībawayh said concerning His saying, Exalted is He: (انْتَهُوا خَيْرًا لَكُمْ); this is stronger with an adverb, even though it is [here] a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The fourth: it is a badal (substitute) from «مَرْيَمَ», a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), because times include bodies; al-Zamakhsharī mentioned this. It is far-fetched, because when a time is neither a ḥāl of a body, nor a khabar (predicate) about it, nor a description of it, it cannot be a badal from it.
It is also said: «إِذْ» has the sense of the maṣdariyya «أَنْ», as when you say "I will not honour you since (إِذْ) you did not honour me", i.e. because you did not honour me; on this view the badal of inclusion is sound, i.e. "and mention Mary, her withdrawing".
And (مَكَانًا): an adverb. It is also said: a mafʿūl bihi according to the meaning, "when she came to a place". (بَشَرًا سَوِيًّا): a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ إِنَّمَا أَنَا رَسُولُ رَبِّكِ لِأَهَبَ لَكِ غُلَامًا زَكِيًّا (١٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِأَهَبَ): it is read with hamza, and concerning it there are two views:
The first: the agent is Allah the Exalted, and the implied form is "He said: that I may grant you".
The second: the agent is Gabriel, peace be upon him; the act was ascribed to him because he is a means in it.
And it is read with yāʾ [«لِيَهَبَ»], and concerning it there are two views:
The first: its origin is the hamza, turned into yāʾ because of the kasra before it, for lightness.
The second: [it means] "that Allah may grant".

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَتْ أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي غُلَامٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ وَلَمْ أَكُ بَغِيًّا () ٢٠).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَغِيًّا): the final radical (lām) of the word is yāʾ; one says «بَغَتْ تَبْغِي». Concerning its pattern there are two views:
The first: it is «فَعُول»; when the wāw and the yāʾ came together, the wāw was turned into yāʾ and assimilated, and the ghayn was given a kasra by assimilation (itbāʿ). For this reason the feminine tāʾ was not attached, just as it is not attached in «امْرَأَةٌ صَبُورٌ» (a patient woman) and «شَكُورٌ» (grateful).
The second: it is «فَعِيل» in the sense of «فَاعِل», and here too the tāʾ was not attached, for intensiveness. It is also said: it was not attached because it is of the relational type (nasab), like «طَالِق» (divorced) and «حَائِض» (menstruating).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ كَذَلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِ هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ وَلِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ وَرَحْمَةً مِنَّا وَكَانَ أَمْرًا مَقْضِيًّا (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكِ): i.e. "the matter is thus".
It is also said: the implied form is "your Lord said the like of that"; and on this view «هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ» is resumptive (mustaʾnaf).
(وَلِنَجْعَلَهُ آيَةً لِلنَّاسِ): i.e. "and in order to make him a sign for people, We created him without a father".
It is also said: the implied form is "We grant him to you, and in order to make him…".
And (كَانَ أَمْرًا): i.e. "and his creation was a matter [decreed]".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَحَمَلَتْهُ فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ مَكَانًا قَصِيًّا (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَانْتَبَذَتْ بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "she withdrew while he was with her".

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَجَاءَهَا الْمَخَاضُ إِلَى جِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَا لَيْتَنِي مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَذَا وَكُنْتُ نَسْيًا مَنْسِيًّا (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَجَاءَهَا الْمَخَاضُ): the origin is «جَاءَهَا»; it was then made transitive by the hamza to a second object, and used in the sense of «أَلْجَأَهَا» (drove her).
And it is read without hamza [«فَاجَاءَهَا»] on the pattern «فَاعَلَهَا», from «الْمُفَاجَأَة» (taking by surprise), the final hamza being dropped for lightness. And «الْمَخَاض», with fatḥa, is the pain of childbirth.
It is also read with kasra; they are two dialectal forms.
It is also said: the fatḥa form is a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), like «السَّلَام» and «الْعَطَاء», and the kasra form is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like «الْقِتَال»; and there have come on the pattern «فِعَال»: «الطِّرَاق» and «الْعِقَاب».
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَالَيْتَنِي): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ.
(نَسِيَا): with kasra, in the sense of «الْمَنْسِيّ» (the forgotten); and with fatḥa, i.e. "a paltry thing", which is close to the meaning of the first.
And it is read with fatḥa on the nūn and a hamza after the sīn [«نَسْئًا»]; this is from «نَسَأْتُ اللَّبَنَ» when you mixed much water into milk; this too has the meaning of the first.
And (مَنْسِيًّا): with fatḥa; the kasra by assimilation (itbāʿ) is irregular (shādhdh), like «الْمِعِيرَة».

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَنَادَاهَا مِنْ تَحْتِهَا أَلًّا تَحْزَنِي قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا (٢٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ تَحْتِهَا): it is read with fatḥa on the mīm [«مَنْ», "the one who"], and it is then the fāʿil (agent) of «نَادَى»; what is meant by it is Jesus ﷺ, i.e. "from beneath her hem". It is also said: what is meant is "from below her". It is also said: what is meant by it is Gabriel, peace be upon him, and he was below her in place, as you say "my house is [below] your house". [Translator's note: the example «دَارِي دَارُكَ» is as written; a fuller form such as «دَارِي تَحْتَ دَارِكَ» may have been intended.] And it is read with kasra on the mīm [«مِنْ», "from"], with the agent latent in the verb, namely Jesus or Gabriel, the blessings of Allah be upon them both; on this view the preposition [and its noun] is a ḥāl (circumstantial) or an adverb (ẓarf).
And (أَنْ لَا): maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), or in the sense of «أَيْ» (that is, explicative).

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَهُزِّي إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ تُسَاقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا (٢٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِجِذْعِ النَّخْلَةِ): the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "bend it towards you". It is also said: it is construed according to the meaning, the implied form being "shake the fruit by means of the trunk", i.e. shake it down. It is also said: the implied form is "and shake towards you fresh ripe dates that are on the trunk of the palm"; on this view the bāʾ [phrase] is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(تُسَاقِطْ): it is read in nine ways: with tāʾ and doubling, the original being «تَتَسَاقَطُ», and that is one of the ways.
[Translator's note: the second way is not stated in the text as it stands; the original «تَتَسَاقَطْ» may be meant.]
The third: with yāʾ and doubling, the original being «يَتَسَاقَطُ», the tāʾ having been assimilated into the sīn.
The fourth: with tāʾ and the light form, by dropping the second [tāʾ]. The agent on these ways is the palm; it is also said: the fruit, because the context indicates both.
The fifth: with tāʾ, the light form, and ḍamma on the qāf.
The sixth: likewise, except that it is with yāʾ; the agent is the trunk or the fruit.
The seventh: «تُسَاقِطْ», with a tāʾ bearing ḍamma, with alif and kasra on the qāf.
The eighth: likewise, except that it is with yāʾ.
The ninth: «تُسْقِطْ», with a tāʾ bearing ḍamma and kasra on the qāf, without alif; and I think it is also read thus with yāʾ.
And (رُطَبًا): concerning it there are four views. The first: it is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa), the one it describes being the pronoun in the verb. The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «تُسَاقِطْ». The third: it is the object of «هُزِّي». The fourth: it is a tamyīz (specification). The details of these views become clear by examining the readings, each of them being taken according to what suits it.
And (جَنِيًّا): in the sense of «مَجْنِيّ» (gathered). It is also said: it is in the sense of the active participle, i.e. "fresh".

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَكُلِي وَاشْرَبِي وَقَرِّي عَيْنًا فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ الْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِي إِنِّي نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ الْيَوْمَ إِنْسِيًّا (٢٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَقَرِّي): it is read with fatḥa on the qāf, and its past is «قَرِرْتِ يَا عَيْنُ» (be cool, O eye), with kasra on the rāʾ. The kasra [on the qāf] is an irregular reading (shādhdh), and it is an irregular dialectal form, its past being «قَرَرْتِ يَا عَيْنُ», with fatḥa on the rāʾ.
And (عَيْنًا): a tamyīz (specification).
And (تَرَيِنَّ): its original is «تَرْأَيِينَ», like «تَرْغَبِينَ»; the hamza is the middle radical (ʿayn) of the verb and the yāʾ its final radical (lām). It is indeclinable (mabnī) here because of the nūn of emphasis, like «لَتَضْرِبَنَّ». The vowel of the hamza was transferred to the rāʾ, and the final radical was dropped because of the indeclinability, just as it is dropped in the jussive; the yāʾ of the pronoun remained and was given a vowel because of its being quiescent and the nūn after it being quiescent. So its pattern is «تَفَيِنَّ». The hamza of this verb is always dropped in the imperfect.
And it is read «تَرَيْنَ», with sukūn on the yāʾ and a light nūn, on the basis that it was not made jussive by «إِمَّا»; this is far-fetched.
And (مِنَ الْبَشَرِ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أَحَدًا», or a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَتَتْ بِهِ قَوْمَهَا تَحْمِلُهُ قَالُوا يَا مَرْيَمُ لَقَدْ جِئْتِ شَيْئًا فَرِيًّا (٢٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَتَتْ بِهِ): the preposition and its genitive noun are a ḥāl (circumstantial); likewise «تَحْمِلُهُ», and the one the ḥāl describes is Mary.
«تَحْمِلُهُ» may also be made a ḥāl from the pronoun of Jesus, peace be upon him. And (جِئْتِ): i.e. "you have done", so «شَيْئًا» is an object. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a grave coming".

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَشَارَتْ إِلَيْهِ قَالُوا كَيْفَ نُكَلِّمُ مَنْ كَانَ فِي الْمَهْدِ صَبِيًّا (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ كَانَ): «كَانَ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "one who is in the cradle". And (صَبِيًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in the preposition [phrase]; the implied detached pronoun [«هُوَ»] was [originally] attached to «كَانَ».
It is also said: the redundant «كَانَ» has no pronoun latent in it; on this view there is no need to assume «هُوَ»; rather the adverbial phrase is the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ». It is also said: it is not redundant, but is like His saying: (وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا), and this has been mentioned. It is also said: it is in the sense of «صَارَ» (became). It is also said: it is the complete [verb] (tāmma), and «مَنْ» means «الَّذِي». It is also said: [«مَنْ» is] conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb) is «كَيْفَ».

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَبَرًّا بِوَالِدَتِي وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْنِي جَبَّارًا شَقِيًّا (٣٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَبَرًّا): conjoined to «مُبَارَكًا». It is read, among the irregular readings (shādhdh), with kasra on the bāʾ and the rāʾ [«وَبِرٍّ»], conjoined to (الصَّلَاةِ).
And it is read with kasra on the bāʾ and fatḥa on the rāʾ [«وَبِرًّا»], i.e. "and He enjoined dutifulness on me", or "You made me possessed of dutifulness", the muḍāf (first term of the construct) being omitted; or he was described by the maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيَّ يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ وَيَوْمَ أَمُوتُ وَيَوْمَ أُبْعَثُ حَيًّا (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالسَّلَامُ): this one comes with the article (alif and lām) only because the one in the story of John (Yaḥyā), peace be upon him, is indefinite; so what is meant by the second is the first, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَى فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا فَعَصَى فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ).
It is also said: the indefinite and the definite are equal in a case like this.
And (يَوْمَ وُلِدْتُ): an adverb (ẓarf), governed by the khabar (predicate), which is «عَلَيَّ». «السَّلَام» does not govern it, because of the separation between them by the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:34-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ الَّذِي فِيهِ يَمْتَرُونَ (٣٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «عِيسَى» its khabar (predicate); «ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ» is a naʿt (adjective) or a second khabar.
And (قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ) [in the nominative]: likewise.
It is also said: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. It is also said: «عِيسَى», peace be upon him, is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and «قَوْلُ الْحَقِّ» is the khabar.
And it is read (قَوْلَ الْحَقِّ) in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), or [as] "I say the word of truth". It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «عِيسَى». It is also said: the implied form is "I mean: the word of truth".
And it is read «قَالَ الْحَقَّ», «الْقَال» being a noun of the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), like «الْقِيل». It is also reported: «قُولَ الْحَقِّ», with ḍamma on the qāf, like «الرُّوح»; this is a dialectal form of it.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ رَبِّي وَرَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُوهُ هَذَا صِرَاطٌ مُسْتَقِيمٌ (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ): with fatḥa on the hamza; concerning it there are two views. The first: it is conjoined to his saying «بِالصَّلَاةِ», i.e. "and He enjoined on me that Allah is my Lord". The second: it is attached to what follows it, the implied form being "because Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him", i.e. obey Him because of His oneness.
And it is read with kasra, as a new sentence (istiʾnāf).

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا لَكِنِ الظَّالِمُونَ الْيَوْمَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ (٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ): its form is the form of the imperative, and its meaning is wonder (taʿajjub). «بِهِمْ» is in the position of the nominative, as when you say «أَحْسِنْ بِزَيْدٍ» (how good Zayd is!), i.e. "Zayd has become good". It is reported from al-Zajjāj that it is a true imperative, the preposition and its genitive noun being in the accusative and the agent latent; it is the pronoun of the speaker, as though the speaker were saying to himself: "bring hearing — or praise — to bear upon him".
And (الْيَوْمَ): an adverb (ẓarf), governed by the adverbial phrase after it.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَنْذِرْهُمْ يَوْمَ الْحَسْرَةِ إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ وَهُمْ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قُضِيَ الْأَمْرُ): «إِذْ» is a badal (substitute) from «يَوْم», or an adverb (ẓarf) for «الْحَسْرَة»; it [«الْحَسْرَة»] is a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the article, and it has governed.

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ يَا أَبَتِ لِمَ تَعْبُدُ مَا لَا يَسْمَعُ وَلَا يُبْصِرُ وَلَا يُغْنِي عَنْكَ شَيْئًا (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ): concerning «إِذْ» there are two views. The first: it is like (إِذِ انْتَبَذَتْ) in its [various] views, and the two have been separated by His saying: (إِنَّهُ كَانَ صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا). The second: «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf), governed by «صِدِّيقًا نَبِيًّا», or by its meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ أَرَاغِبٌ أَنْتَ عَنْ آلِهَتِي يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ لَأَرْجُمَنَّكَ وَاهْجُرْنِي مَلِيًّا (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَرَاغِبٌ أَنْتَ): [«رَاغِبٌ» is] a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أَنْتَ» is a fāʿil (agent) which dispenses with the khabar (predicate); beginning with an indefinite noun is permissible because it leans on the hamza [of interrogation]. And (مَلِيًّا): an adverb (ẓarf), i.e. "a long time". It is also said: it is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا اعْتَزَلَهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَهَبْنَا لَهُ إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا نَبِيًّا (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكُلًّا جَعَلْنَا): it is accusative by «جَعَلْنَا».

ukberi-tibyan:52-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَنَادَيْنَاهُ مِنْ جَانِبِ الطُّورِ الْأَيْمَنِ وَقَرَّبْنَاهُ نَجِيًّا (٥٢) وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ مِنْ رَحْمَتِنَا أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ نَبِيًّا (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَجِيًّا): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (هَارُونَ) is a badal (substitute), and (نَبِيًّا) a ḥāl.

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا (٥٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا): an adverb (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:58-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ النَّبِيِّينَ مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ وَمِمَّنْ حَمَلْنَا مَعَ نُوحٍ وَمِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْرَائِيلَ وَمِمَّنْ هَدَيْنَا وَاجْتَبَيْنَا إِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُ الرَّحْمَنِ خَرُّوا سُجَّدًا وَبُكِيًّا (٥٨) فَخَلَفَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ خَلْفٌ أَضَاعُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَاتَّبَعُوا الشَّهَوَاتِ فَسَوْفَ يَلْقَوْنَ غَيًّا (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ ذُرِّيَّةِ آدَمَ): it is a badal (substitute) from «النَّبِيِّينَ», with the preposition repeated.
And (سُجَّدًا): an anticipated ḥāl (ḥāl muqaddara), because they are not prostrating at the moment of their falling down.
And (بُكِيًّا): this has been mentioned.
And (غَيًّا): its original is «غَوْي»; the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ. [Translator's note: the source prints «غَوَى»; the form with a quiescent wāw, «غَوْي», is what the assimilation presupposes.]

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ الَّتِي وَعَدَ الرَّحْمَنُ عِبَادَهُ بِالْغَيْبِ إِنَّهُ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَأْتِيًّا (٦١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ): whoever gives the tāʾ a kasra makes it a badal (substitute) from «الْجَنَّة» in the verse before it; whoever puts it in the nominative, it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject).
(إِنَّهُ): the hāʾ is the pronoun of the name of Allah the Exalted; it may also be the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn). On the first [view] it is possible that there is no pronoun in «كَانَ», and possible that there is a pronoun in it; and «وَعْدُهُ» is a badal from it, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).
And (مَأْتِيًّا): in its usual sense, because what you come to also comes to you. It is also said: what is meant by the promise is Paradise, i.e. "the thing promised by Him was reached". It is also said: the passive participle (mafʿūl) here has the sense of the active participle (fāʿil); the like of it has been mentioned in [Sūrat] Subḥān [al-Isrāʾ].

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ إِلَّا بِأَمْرِ رَبِّكَ لَهُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِينَا وَمَا خَلْفَنَا وَمَا بَيْنَ ذَلِكَ وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا نَتَنَزَّلُ): i.e. "and the angels say: …".

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فَاعْبُدْهُ وَاصْطَبِرْ لِعِبَادَتِهِ هَلْ تَعْلَمُ لَهُ سَمِيًّا (٦٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ): the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is «فَاعْبُدُوهُ», according to the view of al-Akhfash on the permissibility of a redundant fāʾ. [Translator's note: the source quotes «فَاعْبُدُوهُ»; the verse has «فَاعْبُدْهُ».]

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَقُولُ الْإِنْسَانُ أَإِذَا مَا مِتُّ لَسَوْفَ أُخْرَجُ حَيًّا (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَإِذَا): what governs it is a verb indicated by the context, i.e. "shall I be raised when…?". «أُخْرَجُ» cannot govern it, because what comes after the lām and «سَوْفَ» does not govern what precedes them, like «إِنَّ».

ukberi-tibyan:67-68.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَوَلَا يَذْكُرُ الْإِنْسَانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَلَمْ يَكُ شَيْئًا (٦٧) فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّيَاطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَذَّكَّرُ): with doubling, i.e. «يَتَذَكَّرُ» (reflect); and with the light form [«يَذْكُرُ»], likewise from it, or from mentioning with the tongue.
(جِثِيًّا): this has been mentioned under «عِتِيًّا» and «بُكِيًّا». Its original is «جُثُوّ», whether it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) or a plural.

ukberi-tibyan:69-69.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمَنِ عِتِيًّا (٦٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ): it is read irregularly (shādhdh) in the accusative [«أَيَّهُمْ»], governed by «لَنَنْزِعَنَّ», and it [«أَيّ»] has the sense of «الَّذِي» (the one who).
And it is read with ḍamma, concerning which there are two positions:
The first: it is a ḍamma of indeclinability (bināʾ), and this is the doctrine of Sībawayh. It has the sense of «الَّذِي», and it is made indeclinable here only because indeclinability is its original state, since it stands in the place of «الَّذِي».
«أَيّ» is one of the relative nouns, except that it was made declinable by analogy with «كُلّ» or «بَعْض». So when it is connected with a complete clause it remains declinable, and when the pronoun returning to it is omitted it becomes indeclinable, because it then differs from the rest of the relative nouns; so it returns to its due of indeclinability by departing from its counterparts. Its position is accusative by «نَنْزِعُ».
The second position: it is a ḍamma of declension (iʿrāb), and concerning this there are five views:
The first: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «أَشَدُّ» its khabar (predicate), and it is by way of quotation (ḥikāya); the implied form is "We shall surely draw out from every sect the group of whom it is said: which of them [is most severe]?". On this view it is an interrogative; this is the view of al-Khalīl.
The second: the same, in its being mubtadaʾ and khabar and interrogative, except that the position of the clause is accusative by «نَنْزِعَنَّ», which is a verb suspended (muʿallaq) from governing; its meaning is distinguishing, so it is close to the meaning of knowing, which may be suspended, as when you say "I knew which of them is in the house". This is the view of Yūnus.
The third: the clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), «أَيّ» is interrogative, and «مِنْ» is redundant, i.e. "We shall surely draw out every sect". This is the view of al-Akhfash and al-Kisāʾī, both of whom allow «مِنْ» to be redundant in an affirmative statement.
The fourth: «أَيُّهُمْ» is made nominative by «شِيعَة», because its meaning is "to take sides"; the implied form is "We shall surely draw out from every group which sides [with one another] whichever of them…", and on this view it has the sense of «الَّذِي». This is the view of al-Mubarrad.
The fifth: «نَنْزِعُ» is suspended from governing because the meaning of the sentence is the meaning of a condition, and a condition is not governed by what precedes it. The implied form is "We shall surely draw them out, whether they took sides or did not take sides", or "if they took sides"; like it is "I shall surely beat whichever of them is angry", i.e. whether they are angry or not angry. This is the view [transmitted] by Yaḥyā from al-Farrāʾ, and it is the furthest of them from being correct.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وَارِدُهَا كَانَ عَلَى رَبِّكَ حَتْمًا مَقْضِيًّا (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ): i.e. "and there is not one of you…"; the described noun (mawṣūf) was omitted.
It is also said: the implied form is "and there is none of you but one who will come to it"; its counterparts have preceded.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ قَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَيُّ الْفَرِيقَيْنِ خَيْرٌ مَقَامًا وَأَحْسَنُ نَدِيًّا (٧٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَقَامًا): it is read with fatḥa, and concerning it there are two views:
The first: it is the place of residing. The second: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of residing.
And with ḍamma [«مُقَامًا»], with the same two views.
The final radical (lām) of «النَّدِيّ» is wāw; one says «نَدَوْتُهُمْ», i.e. "I came to their assembly (nādī)" and "I sat in the assembly"; its maṣdar is «النَّدْو».

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ هُمْ أَحْسَنُ أَثَاثًا وَرِئْيًا (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَكَمْ): accusative by «أَهْلَكْنَا», and «هُمْ أَحْسَنُ» is an adjective (ṣifa) of «كَمْ».
And (رئيا): it is read with a quiescent hamza after the rāʾ [«رِئْيًا»]; it is from «الرُّؤْيَة» (seeing), i.e. "better in appearance". And it is read with a doubled yāʾ without hamza [«رِيًّا»], concerning which there are two views:
The first: he turned the hamza into yāʾ because of its being quiescent and preceded by a kasra, and then assimilated it. The second: it is from «الرِّيّ» (being well watered), the opposite of thirst, because it brings about a fine complexion.
And it is read «رِيئًا», with a hamza after a quiescent yāʾ; this is a metathesis (maqlūb), [as] one says «أَرَى» for «رَأَى». [Translator's note: the source wording is «يُقَالُ: فِي رَأَى أَرَى», i.e. "one says, for «رَأَى», «أَرَى»".]
And it is read with a light yāʾ without hamza [«رِيًا»]; its explanation is that he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the yāʾ and dropped it.
And it is read with zāy and doubling [«زِيًّا»], i.e. "better in adornment"; its origin is from «زَوَّى يُزَوِّي», because the one who adorns himself gathers what beautifies him.

ukberi-tibyan:75-76.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ مَنْ كَانَ فِي الضَّلَالَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ لَهُ الرَّحْمَنُ مَدًّا حَتَّى إِذَا رَأَوْا مَا يُوعَدُونَ إِمَّا الْعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا السَّاعَةَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ هُوَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَأَضْعَفُ جُنْدًا (٧٥) وَيَزِيدُ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اهْتَدَوْا هُدًى وَالْبَاقِيَاتُ الصَّالِحَاتُ خَيْرٌ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ ثَوَابًا وَخَيْرٌ مَرَدًّا (٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلْ مَنْ كَانَ): it is conditional, and the command is its apodosis (jawāb). The command here has the sense of a statement, i.e. "He will extend to him"; the command is more emphatic because of the necessity it implies.
And (حَتَّى): here it introduces what follows it [as a new sentence], and it is not attached to a verb.
(إِمَّا الْعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا السَّاعَةَ): both are a badal (substitute) from «مَا يُوعَدُونَ».
(فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ): the apodosis of «إِذَا».
(وَيَزِيدُ): conjoined to the meaning of «فَلْيَمْدُدْ», i.e. "He extends and He increases".
(مَنْ هُوَ): concerning it there are two views. The first: it has the sense of «الَّذِي», and «هُوَ شَرٌّ» is its ṣila (relative clause); the position of «مَنْ» is accusative by «يَعْلَمُونَ». The second: it is interrogative, and «هُوَ» is a separating pronoun (faṣl), not a mubtadaʾ (subject).

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَرَأَيْتَ الَّذِي كَفَرَ بِآيَاتِنَا وَقَالَ لَأُوتَيَنَّ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَوَلَدًا): it is read with fatḥa on the wāw and the lām, and it is singular; it is also said: it may be plural as well. And it is read with ḍamma on the wāw and sukūn on the lām [«وُلْدًا»]; it is the plural of «وَلَد», like «أَسَد» and «أُسْد». It is also said: it may be singular as well, and this is a dialectal form; the kasra [«وِلْد»] is another dialectal form.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَطَّلَعَ الْغَيْبَ أَمِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَطَّلَعَ): the hamza is the hamza of interrogation, because it is paired with «أَمْ»; the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) is dropped because the hamza of interrogation takes its place.
And it is read with kasra [«اطَّلَعَ»], on the basis that it is a connecting hamza, the particle of interrogation being omitted because «أَمْ» indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:79-82.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَلَّا سَنَكْتُبُ مَا يَقُولُ وَنَمُدُّ لَهُ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ مَدًّا (٧٩) وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ وَيَأْتِينَا فَرْدًا (٨٠) وَاتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ آلِهَةً لِيَكُونُوا لَهُمْ عِزًّا (٨١) كَلَّا سَيَكْفُرُونَ بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ وَيَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ ضِدًّا (٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَلَّا): it is read with fatḥa on the kāf and without tanwīn; it is a particle whose meaning is rebuke for a reprehensible statement preceding it. It is also said: it has the sense of «حَقًّا» (truly).
And it is read with tanwīn [«كَلًّا»], concerning which there are two views. The first: it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «كَلَّ», i.e. "became exhausted", i.e. they became exhausted in their claim and were cut short. The second: it has the sense of a burden, i.e. "they carried a burden".
And it is read with ḍamma on the kāf and with tanwīn [«كُلًّا»]; it is then a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "they will all disbelieve"; and this is far-fetched.
(بِعِبَادَتِهِمْ): the maṣdar is annexed to the agent, i.e. "the idolaters will disavow their worship of the idols".
It is also said: it is annexed to the object, i.e. "the idolaters will disavow the worship of the idols".
It is also said: [it means] "the devils will disavow the idolaters' worship of them".
And (ضِدًّا): a singular with the meaning of a plural. The meaning is that all of them have a single status, because they are agreed on leading astray.
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَنَرِثُهُ مَا يَقُولُ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it is a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), i.e. "We shall inherit his saying". The second: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "We shall inherit from him his saying".

ukberi-tibyan:85-87.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ الْمُتَّقِينَ إِلَى الرَّحْمَنِ وَفْدًا (٨٥) وَنَسُوقُ الْمُجْرِمِينَ إِلَى جَهَنَّمَ وِرْدًا (٨٦) لَا يَمْلِكُونَ الشَّفَاعَةَ إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ عِنْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ عَهْدًا (٨٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَوْمَ نَحْشُرُ): what governs it is «لَا يَمْلِكُونَ»; it is also said: «نَعُدُّ لَهُمْ».
It is also said: its implied form is "mention".
And (وَفْدًا): the plural of «وَافِد» (one coming as a delegate), like «رَاكِب» and «رَكْب», and «صَاحِب» and «صَحْب». «الْوِرْد» is a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for «وَارِد» (one coming to water). It is also said: it has the sense of «وَارِد», «الْوِرْد» being the thirsty ones. It is also said: it is shortened from «وِرَاد», which is far-fetched. (لَا يَمْلِكُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial). And (إِلَّا مَنِ اتَّخَذَ): in the position of the accusative as a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also said: it is connected (muttaṣil), on the basis that the pronoun in «يَمْلِكُونَ» refers to the God-fearing and the criminals. It is also said: it is in the position of the nominative as a badal (substitute) from the pronoun in «يَمْلِكُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:89-89.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إِدًّا (٨٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (شَيْئًا إِدًّا): the majority [read] with kasra on the hamza; it means "the monstrous".
It is read irregularly (shādhdh) with fatḥa on it [«أَدًّا»], on the basis that it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَدَّ يَؤُدُّ», when he brought you a calamity, i.e. "a thing possessing calamity"; and He made it the calamity itself, by way of magnification.

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تَكَادُ السَّمَاوَاتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنْهُ وَتَنْشَقُّ الْأَرْضُ وَتَخِرُّ الْجِبَالُ هَدًّا (٩٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَتَفَطَّرْنَ): it is read with yāʾ and nūn [«يَنْفَطِرْنَ»], which is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of «فَطَرَ» with the light form. And it is read with tāʾ and doubling, which is the reflexive of «فَطَّرَ» with the doubled form; and here this is closer to the meaning.
And (هَدًّا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to the meaning, because «تَخِرُّ» has the sense of «تُهَدُّ» (is demolished). It is also said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَنْ دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَنِ وَلَدًا (٩١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ دَعَوْا لِلرَّحْمَنِ): concerning it there are three views. The first: it is in the position of the accusative, because it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The second: in the position of the genitive, with the lām implied. The third: in the position of the nominative, i.e. "what brings that about is their ascribing [a son]".

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ كُلُّ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ إِلَّا آتِي الرَّحْمَنِ عَبْدًا (٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ): an indefinite noun that is described (nakira mawṣūfa), and «فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ» is its adjective; «إِلَّا آتِي» is the khabar (predicate) of «كُلُّ». «آتِي» is singular, construed according to the wording of «كُلّ»; it has been made plural elsewhere, construed according to its meaning. An instance of the singular is: (وَكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ).

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لِتُبَشِّرَ بِهِ الْمُتَّقِينَ وَتُنْذِرَ بِهِ قَوْمًا لُدًّا (٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِلِسَانِكَ): it is said: the bāʾ has the sense of «عَلَى» (upon). It is also said: it has its original sense, i.e. "We sent it down in your language", so it is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
